If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is above true value, apply downward bias of 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to align with mean reversion.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 and forecast is below true value, add upward bias of 1–2% for early horizon to capitalize on sentiment-driven breakout.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) across 5+ days, suppress forecast volatility by smoothing 2–3% downward for mid horizon to avoid overreaction.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and true price exceeds forecast by >2%, apply upward correction of 1–3% for late horizon to reflect sentiment lag.
